title: Investigate and Mitigate Prefetch-Admission Interaction Causing GPU Queue Runaway
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a hosted API capacity incident on 2026-03-09 we observed persistent GPU queue growth on multiple pools even after autoscaler triggers. The immediate symptom was long request queuing and token-level latency spikes for multi-tenant customers. Root cause analysis points to an emergent interaction between the tenant prefetch/prewarm subsystem and the admission controller plus a scheduling regression that increased KV-cache eviction rates.
root_cause: A combination of factors: (1) tenant prefetch logic aggressively issued warmup work and kept queued prefetch requests counted against pool admission budget; (2) admission controller used a pool-wide token budget but lacked per-tenant queue-depth gating, allowing one "warmth-seeking" tenant to consume slot reservations; (3) a recent kernel-selection scheduler change (PR #6789) shifted GPU memory allocation patterns causing higher KV-cache churn and intermittent OOM retries which amplified queued requests as prefetches retried; and (4) autoscaler hysteresis was tuned conservatively, preventing timely scale-up during the burst window.
impact_details: - ~12 hosted GPU pools experienced degraded throughput for 22 minutes.
mitigation_so_far:
- Emergency action: disabled cross-tenant prefetching and reduced per-tenant prewarm budget by 80% (rollout 2026-03-09T21:05 UTC).
- Temporarily relaxed autoscaler down-hysteresis to allow faster scale decisions (2026-03-09T21:20 UTC).
- Rolled back kernel-selection change to previous stable commit while we triage (2026-03-09T22:10 UTC).

action_items: Hotfix A (owner: Alex Rivera): Implement per-tenant admission gating to cap queued requests per tenant at pool level. Target: feature flag rollout by 2026-03-18.

Hotfix B (owner: SRE Team): Add fast-path circuit-breaker in admission controller to reject prefetch requests when pool queue > 60% of safe capacity. Document immediate override steps in runbook. Target: 2026-03-14.
Telemetry (owner: Omar Haddad): Add metrics: tenant_queue_depth, prefetch_retry_count, kv_cache_eviction_rate, admission_reject_reasons. Dashboards for oncall. Target: 2026-03-16.
Autoscaler tuning (owner: Priya Patel): Create canary with reduced scale-up hysteresis and test across synthetic load shapes to avoid oscillation. Target: 2026-03-20.

Kernel scheduler follow-up (owner: Runtime Team): Reproduce memory allocation regression introduced in PR #6789 under controlled load and provide patch or revert explanation. Link to test harness: GH: rwin/runtime#bench-ks. Target: 2026-03-22.
E2E test (owner: QA): Add a sustained prefetch-heavy tiered workload to nightly stress tests and a chaos experiment that kills a GPU to validate graceful degradation. Target: 2026-03-25.

Runbook (owner: SRE): Update hosted GPU drain and prefetch emergency runbook with step-by-step toggles, metrics to watch, and escalation matrix. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Prefetch+Emergency+Runbook. Target: 2026-03-15.
